The eighth review of 1.24.36's givens and code checks: what the seventh round of mends (ca567b7) broke
against the round before it (adb8fd7), in src/lantern.inner.html.

Written by a reviewer who had not seen the mends drafted. Read: CLAUDE.md, the diff adb8fd7..ca567b7 of
src/lantern.inner.html, and the GIVENS, GIVENS_CONTROL, CODE_CHECKS and CODE_CHECKS_CONTROL modules as they stand.
Not read: tests/fixtures/givens_review*_1236, code_checks_review_1236, review3..review7_1236, tests/givens_1236.js,
tests/code_checks_1236.js, tests/review*_1236.py.

SUMMARY

288 cases (cases.js), most of them right questions and right circuits that must keep working. Each case says what is
right for its question, not what either version does. replay.js runs them; run_ca567b7.txt is its output on ca567b7.

  ca567b7: 216 AGREE, 72 DISAGREE
  adb8fd7: 246 AGREE, 42 DISAGREE   (same cases, run from git show adb8fd7:src/lantern.inner.html)

  New breaks (adb8fd7 right, ca567b7 wrong): 64 cases -- 49 high, 14 medium, 1 low, in 8 high faults and 5 medium ones
  Old faults (both wrong the same way):       8 cases -- 6 high, 1 medium, 1 low
  Mended by this round (adb8fd7 wrong, ca567b7 right): 34 cases
  Bench guard: every bench prompt (sets A and B, 300) equals 1.24.35's except make-control and make-control-b. AGREE.

NEW BREAKS, HIGH (a given shown that does not fit, or fitted wrong; a circuit sent back that Lantern cannot be
sure is wrong)

H1. A control transformer's DC side is drawn AC.  sup-05 sup-06 sup-08 sup-09 sup-10
    "a 480 V/24 V DC control transformer", "a 120 V AC / 24 V DC control transformer", "control transformer 230 V /
    24 V DC", "control transformer 480 V to 24 V dc" -> supply "24 V AC". adb8fd7 gave no supply line.
    Where: supply(), cp.push({ v: lo, kind: x.kind || "AC", ... }). The kind is taken from the pair's FIRST voltage (x),
    never from the one that was written lower; "DC" written on the lower is lost. ("control transformer 120/24 V DC"
    reads 24 V DC because there x is the 24 V DC itself.) Take the kind from the lower voltage as written, or give no
    supply where DC is said beside a transformer.

H2. An e-stop or a light before "and start/stop ... at two locations" is cut out of the count.
    sta-02 sta-03 sta-05 sta-17 sta-25 sta-26 (e-stop), sta-06 sta-07 (light)
    "a pump starter with an e-stop and start and stop buttons at two locations" -> two stations and ONE e-stop; "a
    conveyor starter with a green run light and start and stop buttons at two locations" -> two stations and ONE light;
    "an e-stop and push buttons at two locations" the same. adb8fd7 gave none (the sixth review: "an e-stop at two
    locations" is not sure).
    Where: stations(), CUT now cuts at "and" before start/stop/push, and the exception for "start and stop" is skipped
    after "e-stop", "estop" and "emergency stop" by design. "At two locations" can belong to the whole list: an e-stop
    at each operator station is the usual practice (NFPA 79's emergency stop section puts one at each operator control
    station -- recalled, not read on a page in this review), and a pilot light on each station is common. This is a
    judgement on scope, so Adam may read it otherwise; by rule 7 two readings give nothing. Note that adb8fd7 already
    gave one e-stop for the comma form ("a motor starter, an e-stop, and start and stop at two locations", sta-24,
    accepted here both ways). "E stop" with a space still gives none (sta-04) -- the forms now disagree.

H3. One stop button for both machines: the sequence given draws a stop for each.
    seq-03 seq-04 seq-07 seq-08 seq-09 seq-10 seq-11
    "...; the stop button stops the conveyors" (the pumps, the fans, the motors), "the stop button stops the first
    conveyor and the second", "a stop button stops the fans", ", and the stop button stops it" -> the sequence given
    (a stop for conveyor 1 and one for conveyor 2). adb8fd7 gave none.
    Where: stopSaid(), the new third replace \b(?:the\s+)?stop ... button\s+stops\s+(?:it|the\s+(?!two|both|all)[\w-]+)
    strips a plural object ("the conveyors"), "a stop button" (the "the" is optional), and "the first" in "the first
    conveyor and the second" (the lookahead sees " conveyor", not "and"). It is right for one machine (the delayed
    start, del-20..22) but the sequence names two: there "the stop button stops ..." says one button.
    seq-11: "conveyor 1 has start, stop and conveyor 2 has start only" -> the given gives conveyor 2 a stop. Where: the
    comma now allowed in the first replace, (?:start|run)[\s\x2F&,-]+(?:and\s+)?stop, strips "start, stop" and nothing
    else in the question says a stop.

H4. A plural with no count: two machines are invented.  seq-25 seq-26 seq-27 seq-28 seq-29 seq-30 seq-31
    "Draw a control circuit for conveyors that start in sequence", "pumps that must start in sequence", "a sequence
    start control circuit for the conveyors", "an interlocked start control circuit for the conveyors", "the fans
    must start in order", "the motor starters", "compressors that start in sequence" -> a sequence of exactly two
    ("conveyor 1", "conveyor 2"). adb8fd7 gave none (machines() was 1, so seqOrder gave nothing).
    Where: machines() now returns 2 for any plural; seqOrder(), with one kind and no order word, then numbers n of them
    (for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) out.push(kd + " " + i)). The plural says "more than one", not "two". Elsewhere the same
    2 is only ever used to refuse (starter, delayed start, compressor, fill, sump), which is safe; in seqOrder it is
    read as the count.

H5. A delay timed from power or from another device: the push-button delayed start is shown.
    del-01 del-02 del-03 del-04 del-05 del-06 del-07 del-08
    "the pump starts 30 seconds after the supply comes on" (the transformer, the control, the panel, the control
    voltage, the machine, the starter, the contactor) -> stop PB1 CR1 / start PB2 CR1 / timer TR1 "30 s" ... -- a start
    button the question never asked for, and no start from power. adb8fd7 refused them.
    Where: the delayed start's asks, /\bcomes?\s+(?:back\s+)?on\b/ became /\bcomes?\s+back\s+on\b/ (to let "a horn
    comes on" through, del-14, del-25 -- those are right now). The new "after the <machine> starts" refusal lists only
    machine words, so supply, transformer, control, panel, voltage, machine, starter and contactor pass (all are
    words the vocabulary knows). "after the main switch comes on" is still refused, by the vocabulary (del-31).

H6. The sump: the pump's own run light makes an alarm light too.
    sump-05 sump-06 sump-07 sump-08 sump-11 sump-12 sump-14 sump-15
    "a sump pump control circuit with a high water alarm horn and a run light" (a pump running light ..., a green
    light while the pump runs, a light that shows the pump is running, a run lamp, a pump on light and a horn for the
    high water alarm, a run light and a high water alarm bell) -> LT1 "pump on" AND LT2 FS2 "high water" red AND the
    horn. No alarm light was asked; adb8fd7 drew the run light and the horn.
    Where: the sump block, al = /lights?...[^.,;]{0,30}(alarm|high water)|(alarm|high water)[^.,;]{0,20}lights?/ --
    any light word within 20-30 characters of "alarm" in the same clause. Asking that the light word itself say
    nothing of its own (no run, running, pump on, on while) before reading it as the alarm's would keep sump-03, -04
    and -13 (mended by this round) and leave these.

H7. Vacuum and negative pressure: switches Lantern cannot judge are sent back again.  chk-01 chk-21 chk-03 chk-22
    "a vac pump with a high vac cut-out" (and "a low vac cut-out" drawn nc), "a blower holding a negative-pressure
    room" (hyphen), with a high or a low pressure cut-out -> sent back "a high cut-out drawn normally open: M1 would
    run only while the pressure is above it", with nc to be added (or taken off). adb8fd7 left them (the sixth
    review: which way a vacuum switch cuts out is not sure).
    Where: way(), \bvac\w* became \bvacuum\b and \bnegative\b became \bnegative\s+(?:pressure|bar|psi|kpa|gauge)\b.
    The aim -- "120 VAC" no longer read as vacuum (chk-05, chk-06, mended) -- is right, but "vac" is the shop word for
    vacuum ("vac pump", "vac switch") and "negative-pressure" is written with a hyphen as often as not. "vac" not
    right after a number (where it is a voltage's unit, "120 VAC"), and [\s-]+ after "negative", would keep both
    (ES5 has no lookbehind: test the characters before the match in code).

H8. A stop relay energised to stop that drops a run relay is sent back.  chk-08 chk-24
    stop PB1 CR1 no / relay CR1 "stop relay" / start PB2 CR2 / relay CR2 CR1 off "run relay" / coil M1 CR2, and a
    delayed start whose stop relay CR3 drops its run relay CR1 -> "PB1 is a stop written normally open: drawn so, the
    circuit runs only while it is held", line "stop PB1 CR1". adb8fd7 left them, as it leaves "coil M1 CR1 off"
    (chk-07, chk-25, chk-26 agree on both). The line back is false of this drawing: nothing runs only while PB1 is
    held. Where: control-stops, the exemption now needs the closed contact in a rung whose output is M\d or a starter.
    The fourth review's rule ("a relay whose contact is used closed in another rung is energised to trip") does not
    depend on what that rung drives; the seventh round's case (a run relay's own stop written open, with only a lamp
    on its closed contact, chk-09) is mended, but narrowing to starters' rungs also takes in relays. Requiring the
    closed contact in a rung of a coil or timer OTHER than the stop's own coil would keep chk-09 and chk-08 both.
    Whether an energise-to-stop relay is acceptable at all (it does not stop on a broken wire) is Adam's to decide;
    this case is high only by the project's own earlier rule.

NEW BREAKS, MEDIUM (a plain question adb8fd7 handled right that ca567b7 now misses, safely)

M1. sta-08 sta-09: "stop buttons and start buttons at two locations", "a stop button and start button at two
    locations" -> no given (adb8fd7: two stations). stations(): the new cut at "and" before "start" leaves "and start
    buttons at two locations", start without stop. (sta-10, "a start and a stop button at two locations", was missed
    by both: old.)
M2. seq-13 seq-14 seq-15 del-19: "each with a start button and a stop button at the panel" ("a stop button for it",
    "a stop button on the conveyor"; the delayed start's "with a stop button at the panel") -> no given. stopSaid(): the
    fourth replace now strips "a stop button" only before the end, a comma, and, or, plus or with.
M3. lit-01 lit-02 lit-04: "a start/stop push button station", "a start-stop pushbutton station", "a start stop button
    station" -> no given. The starter's new not-list entry (?:one|single|a)\s+start[\s\x2F-]+stop\s+(?:push)?button
    (?!s) also takes "a start/stop push button STATION" (two buttons). ("a start/stop button" alone, lit-03, is right to
    refuse.)
M4. lit-26 lit-29: "for motors over 5 hp", "one of the pump starters" -> no given (machines() plural). Most plurals
    are right to refuse (lit-24, -27, -28, -30, sump-21, del-24 mended).
M5. lit-45: "a pilot light, the start button is not illuminated" -> no given (read()'s new lit-button test sees
    "illuminated").
    keep-03 keep-05: a circuit kept for "...start and stop buttons" is no longer shown for "...start and stop button"
    (pushbuttons/pushbutton): said() no longer stems. Safe; keep-04 and keep-10 (fans/fan, compressor/compressors),
    which the stems let through, are mended by the same change.

NEW BREAK, LOW

L1. chk-14: an overload's open contact written to an alarm relay CR2 "pump overload" now draws a second line back
    ("an overload contact written normally open"), on a circuit questioned anyway (CR2 has nothing switching it).
    NOT_MACHINE no longer has "overload" alone, so a relay named "pump overload" is read as a machine.

OLD FAULTS (adb8fd7 and ca567b7 wrong the same way)

  sup-12  high    "a control transformer, 480/240 V motor" -> supply "240 V AC": the motor's pair read as the
                  transformer's (XF_BEFORE takes "control transformer, " before any pair).
  seq-36  high    "so the conveyors can only start after the crusher is running" -> a crusher and ONE conveyor.
  del-09  high    "the fan starts 30 seconds after the machine starts" -> the push-button delayed start ("machine" is
                  not in the new refusal's list).
  del-10  high    "the fan starts 30 seconds after the supply is on" -> the push-button delayed start.
  lit-14  high    "start and stop push buttons, the start is a latching type" -> the momentary three-wire starter.
  lit-22  high    "and a run light; no lights in the buttons" -> the starter WITHOUT the run light (NOLIGHT reads "no
                  lights" anywhere).
  sta-10  medium  "a start and a stop button at two locations" -> no given.
  pick-12 low     "the Zambian mine" -> US (ADJ_IEC has no Zambian or Zimbabwean).

WHAT AGREES

  - The bench guard: only make-control and make-control-b differ from 1.24.35's prompts.
  - supply(): a pair beside "control transformer" in every form tried (480/120 V, 480 V / 120 V, 120 V to 24 V,
    480-120 V, 480 to 120 volt, 480 V : 120 V, control transformer: 480 V / 120 V, 600 V to 120 V, 120 V/24 V), a
    motor's pair set aside and the control's own voltage read (sup-04, -11, -21, -24, -25, -27, -31), a bare lower
    still not sure (sup-16), 480/277 V still none (sup-36).
  - stations(): the plain forms (two locations, both ends, local and remote, three stations, 2 locations, 24 V DC with
    two places, a run light after the count), "a start button and stop buttons at two locations" and "a single start
    at the panel" now refused (mended).
  - The sequence: the plain forms, "each has start, stop buttons", "a start, stop for each", "the stop button stops the
    conveyor it is on" (now given, right), "after conveyor 1, which feeds it, has stopped" now refused (mended), the
    appositive forms (seq-20, -23, -24), three conveyors by number.
  - The delayed start: "a horn comes on for 10 seconds, then the conveyor starts" and "the horn comes on while it
    waits" now given with the horn (right); one machine's "the stop button stops it" now given (right); "the pumps"
    now refused (mended).
  - The starter's not-list: one button that starts and stops, latching push buttons, push again, push to start/push
    to stop, the same push button, "also a stop button at the panel" -- all refused now (mended); lit buttons refused.
  - The sump: "an alarm horn and light", "a horn and a light for high water", "an indicator for high level" now draw
    the alarm light too (mended).
  - The code checks: "120 VAC" no longer hides a compressor's cut-out drawn open (chk-05, -06); a coil named
    "compressor starter, overload relay OL1" or "compressor with overload" is judged (chk-11..13); a run relay's own
    stop written open with a lamp on its closed contact is sent back (chk-09); IEC lines for "Lusaka, Zambia" (chk-20).
  - The code pick: "Lusaka, Zambia", "Harare, Zimbabwe", ", Zambia", "Bulawayo, zimbabwe" -> IEC; Zambia Street, Tulsa
    -> US; "Kitwe, Zambia to NEC" -> US.
  - Kept circuits: the same words, the asking words ("please", "again", "the"), and the colour, voltage and station
    differences all behave.

WHAT WAS NOT RUN

  - No model, small or large: every case is Lantern's own reading (L.aiAct.prompt, L.aiAct.build, L.givens.keep and
    match, L.codeChecks.pick) in jsdom, through tests/fixtures/liftstation_review1_1230/load.js. Whether a model copies
    the wrong blocks above was not tried.
  - Not npm test, not the browser tests, not the bench, not a build of site/ or the bundle.
  - 1.24.35 (8cb3281) was loaded only for the bench guard (guard_1235.json, made by gen_guard.js); it has no givens.
  - The circuits in the build cases were written by this reviewer as a model might write them, not taken from a run.
  - Which practice NFPA 79 asks for e-stops at each operator station (H2) was recalled, not read on a page here.
